column1: # Native source productions reconstructed from the actual reference Ghidra C, with paired classic C/ASM retained for edition-specific source details. This is a source catalogue, not a test or observed game result.
# Main functions are reference RVAs; paired classic roots are identified by native-rtti.tsv. Function C files retain every native condition, including null/invalid branches and empty output.

# Notation: quoted text retains its literal spacing; + is byte concatenation and adds no separator; ε emits nothing; [] marks a conditional suffix, with its condition in the row. Named nonterminals are expanded in other rows of the same type. TITLE means the preceding main/continuation production.

# DATE is the shared history-date supplier b92640: year<1="a time before time"; tick=-1=signed YEAR; otherwise "the "+PHASE+SEASON+" of "+YEAR, PHASE="early "/"mid"/"late ", SEASON=spring/summer/autumn/winter or empty for out-of-range season. No implied game-observation claim.

# Shared leaves: HF=history-figure b92f10 (style shown where material); ENTITY=b92900; SITE=b93930; REGION=b94a40; UG=b94940; BUILDING=b94090; CONSTRUCTION=b93a90; ARTIFACT=b94400; RAW_CREATURE=b94ed0; REASON=b5a6c0. Each retains its native name/unknown/nullable branches in the supplier C files.

# LIST(HF) uses native comma/and separators; FOCUSED_LIST emits context-HF first, the other HF for a two-member list, or " and others" for >2. Reverse lists explicitly say REVERSE_LIST. These are typed lists, not arbitrary English fields.

# The actual STORY_EVENT popup initializes context+24=-1 and flags=0. The figure helper's first-person I/me/my/myself paths are therefore unreachable in this popup; style2 uses the ordinary possessive identity here.
